when_to_use: cinematic noir jazz where silence, decay, and one mournful call carry more narrative weight than harmonic motion, muted trumpet over dark piano, 42-50 BPM
style: cinematic noir jazz / dark-jazz scene score

defaults.feel: ultra-dragged/rubato - only the brushed-snare swirl stays near the grid, everything else floats behind it

signature_moves: the detective's walk: Am(maj7) -> Am7 -> Am6 -> Fmaj7(#11) -> E7(b9,b13), letting one tonic identity deteriorate step by step
the rainy alleyway: Cm9 -> Fm9 -> Abmaj7(#11) -> G7alt, moving through shadowed rooms without increasing harmonic speed
cluster friction voicing: place semitone tension inside the chord so discomfort is heard as proximity, not volume (see noir-jazz-genre.md SS4)
cadence_options: altered dominant resolution: E7(b9,b13) -> Am(maj7), arriving at a tonic that still carries damage inside it
no hard cadence when the truest ending is decay, unanswered space, or a scene disappearing before resolution
avoid: plain bright major colors; replace them with maj7#11 or m(maj7) so even consonance retains a shadow
dense or fast harmonic rhythm; every chord needs enough time to become atmosphere and then become absence

hook_archetypes.name: three-notes-in-the-rain
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a short 3-note muted-trumpet call across 1-2 bars, followed by silence long enough for the answer to feel uncertain
hook_archetypes.contour: bend or slide upward into b5 or b3 from below, then let the final tone weaken rather than resolve
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Scene 2, answered only by one low piano chord several beats later

hook_archetypes.name: room-after-the-chord
hook_archetypes.rhythm: strike one chord and let its full decay become the phrase; do not restrike until the silence itself has changed character
hook_archetypes.contour: use Am(maj7) or a close cluster whose inner friction remains audible after the attack disappears
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Scene 1, the first piano entrance after the bass has already established emptiness

alleyway-intro.note_lengths: near silence: one bass pluck every 2 bars and one chord allowed to decay across several bars
alleyway-intro.contour: n/a; the absence of melody establishes the world before any character enters

shadow-theme.note_lengths: short mournful calls, occasional long notes, and more silence than statement
shadow-theme.contour: blue-note bends enter the target from below, with the final pitch allowed to remain emotionally compromised
shadow-theme.placement: extremely dragged behind the brushed swirl

confession-interlude.note_lengths: sparse duet phrases where sax and piano rarely speak at the same moment
confession-interlude.contour: low sub-tone tenor lines, breath-forward and reluctant, with piano answers that reveal rather than decorate
confession-interlude.placement: the same deep drag, with trumpet absent so the scene acquires a different witness

resolution-outro.note_lengths: restate only enough of the theme for recognition, then remove notes until one bass pluck and one final chord remain
resolution-outro.contour: let the last statement descend or thin, avoiding a heroic final interval
resolution-outro.placement: drag increases as the scene loses momentum and disappears into silence

drum_skeleton.low_energy: constant soft brushed-snare swirl only, no kick, with an occasional ride bloom on beat 1 that fades before becoming pulse
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: keep the swirl fragile; add a near-inaudible felt kick and sparse ride responses so the scene gains presence without confidence
drum_skeleton.high_energy: do not become louder; the ceiling is a fuller trio texture, with tension created by additional witnesses and closer interaction rather than harder hits

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: Scene 1 begins with absence: bass, then one decaying piano chord. Scene 2 introduces the brushed swirl and muted-trumpet call, making the first melody feel like evidence. Scene 3 removes trumpet and gives tenor sax the confession, with piano answering from a distance. Scene 4 must empty the frame completely by dropping drums and bass, leaving only a tail and one delayed tone. Scene 5 permits the ensemble to restate the theme, but the ending must reduce everything back to one pluck, one chord, and no explanation.

anti_boredom_rules: leave every chord enough time to decay into a new texture before the next attack; harmonic patience is the primary source of tension
remove roughly half the melody a conventional first draft would include; silence must carry narrative information
one full scene must drop drums and bass entirely so the listener feels the floor disappear
dynamics remain ppp-pp; narrative escalation must come from proximity, register, timbre, and the order of entrances
the three-note call must return with a changed register, answer, silence length, or speaker
ambient texture is optional and subordinate; it must never become the event that the instruments should create

bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: floats behind the brushed reference and may disappear for an entire scene
bass_behavior.density: one note every one or two bars
bass_behavior.articulation: dark upright plucks with full decay

groove_intent.feel: near-rubato cinematic drag around a soft brush reference
groove_intent.kick: absent or nearly inaudible felt accents
groove_intent.snare: continuous quiet brush swirl rather than backbeat
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: all pitched voices float behind the brush and use silence as structural material

distinguishing_traits: scene-based cinematic narrative rather than song or solo form
extreme ppp-pp space and two-bar chord decay
near-rubato placement with complete rhythm-section drop in the fog scene
